prize_parts.citation: for the invention of the optical lattice clock, in which magic-wavelength trapping allows many neutral atoms to be interrogated at once free of light shift, and for its development to a fractional uncertainty of about 1e-18

statement.case_for: I keep B059 with Katori and Ye. Having heard the whole first round, the case rests on three things I can state without leaning on opening support. First, the lattice clock is different in kind from the comb (2005) and single-ion (2012) prizes: those recognised a frequency ruler and control of one quantum system, while Katori's magic-wavelength condition lets thousands of neutral atoms be held and interrogated together with the clock-transition light shift cancelled, which is what moved statistical stability and then accuracy to about 1e-18. Second, as an instrument builder I judge a metrology claim by whether independent laboratories reproduce and compare it, and strontium and ytterbium lattice clocks do, with comparisons, relativistic geodesy and limits on varying constants as concrete products. Third, Ye's group carried the concept to the accuracy frontier and added many-body and spin-polarised-fermion physics, so the two names correspond to the proposal and the frontier realisation. I accept Lindroth's and Kroll's point that the case must stand on demonstrated performance, not on a future redefinition of the second.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a real objection and I cannot dismiss it by argument alone; it can only be managed by a narrow citation. The two-name credit leaves out Lemonde, the SYRTE and PTB groups, Takamoto and the NIST/JILA team beyond Ye, whose milestones are intertwined with the 1e-18 result, and nobody in round 1 identified a distinct conceptual contribution that would justify a third name. B016 is a larger change in how electronic matter is classified, and a committee that values conceptual reclassification over a measurement capability could reasonably rank it first. Finally I am the chair and moved to B059 after the opening ballots, so my support should not be counted as independent evidence of merit.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B016 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, because it opened a new conceptual category and not a better measurement, and asks whether the lattice clock is a refinement of comb and ion-clock metrology.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my position and I give it real weight. My answer is that the lattice clock rests on a distinct idea, the magic-wavelength condition, which has no counterpart in the comb or the single-ion clock, and it changed the statistical regime by interrogating many atoms at once. I do not claim that this equals the conceptual reach of a new classification of band insulators. Where I still differ is on what the committee can defend: the B016 trio leaves out Hasan and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the committee has not argued that exclusion through. I would accept B016 as the final prize if members who prefer it agree on a citation that states the limit explicitly, and I would not treat that outcome as a failure.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B016, rebuts the 2016-overlap worry, notes that HgTe transport is demanding and that most broad confirmation is in 3D materials, and says she would not object to B059 if the committee prefers a tightly attributed two-person prize.
responses.response: Her qualification that the independent confirmation lies mostly in 3D materials, which the proposed citation does not credit, sharpens the attribution problem for B016 and makes me more cautious about calling its confirmation record stronger than that of the clocks. I agree that the 2016 prize does not cover Z2 insulators, so I withdraw any weight on overlap there. I also take her point that a clock's significance is partly measured by what it enables; I accept that part of the payoff is prospective, and that is why I want the citation to cite the demonstrated accuracy only. I am glad to hear that she would not object to B059, and I would say the same of B016.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B034, separates a settled mechanism from a settled discovery, and says B059's reach is partly prospective and not more decisive than a new correlated-matter platform.
responses.response: His distinction between mechanism and discovery is fair and the Prize has honoured discoveries before their mechanism was understood. My difficulty is different: the experimental credit. Yuan Cao and the other first authors of the 2018 papers are outside the trio, the field is still moving quickly, and Jarillo-Herrero's group is credited for experiments whose key results were largely led by others. I find that harder to defend than the Katori-Ye split, and I do not think a narrow citation on flat bands and observed states removes the credit problem. I keep B034 as an alternative and would support it in a later year.

responses.point: Kroll supports B059 and argues that magic-wavelength trapping is an idea about atom-light interaction, so the lattice clock differs in regime from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and that a third name would be arbitrary.
responses.response: I agree and have adopted his formulation in the citation, which now names magic-wavelength trapping and interrogation of many atoms. I also accept his refusal to rely on the redefinition of the second. I do not think his disclosed stay in Hall's laboratory is disqualifying, but because we both support B059 the committee should weigh our two positions with that in mind, and I note that this applies to my own preference as well.

responses.point: Lindroth supports B059, argues that systematics control and parallel interrogation distinguish it, and asks that the novelty claim be checked against the primary literature and not recollection.
responses.response: I agree with the request, and it is the main test of the position. The relevant check is that the 2005 prize cited comb-based optical frequency measurement and the 2012 prize cited control and measurement of individual quantum systems, while neither cited a neutral-atom lattice with the light shift engineered away. I cannot verify that from the supplied material beyond my recollection, so I state it as a belief and not a settled fact. I also have no distinct lattice-clock contribution that would justify a third name beyond Katori and Ye, and I do not expect one to emerge.

responses.point: Johansson prefers B013, concedes its closeness to the 2025 circuit prize and the omission of Girvin, and notes lattice clocks as a second-tier option that he would not oppose.
responses.response: I accept that circuit QED is distinct from the 2025 work in what it rewards, coupling to a single photon in a resonator, and I do not doubt its importance. His own account of the Girvin omission and of the timing, together with the disclosed conflict at Chalmers, leaves it harder to bring to a final vote than B059 or B016, and I would prefer to see it considered again in a later year than this one.

uncertainties: Whether the lattice clock is judged distinct in kind from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, which I believe it is but cannot settle from supplied material.

Whether the committee ranks a measurement capability (B059) above a classification of electronic matter (B016), where the evidence on maturity is comparable and the real difference is conceptual breadth against attribution.
Whether leaving out Lemonde and other lattice-clock groups is acceptable, since none has yet been shown to have a distinct conceptual contribution.
How much weight my own move from B043 to B059 and Kroll's connection to Hall's laboratory should carry in the committee's reading of support for B059.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B059, B016 or B034, and I have no documented tie to Katori, Ye or their groups. My astroparticle and gamma-ray work (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) is close to B043, and my CERN-based PhD is close to B019; I claim no recusal need on either and neither is part of my final position. I note Kroll's disclosure on B059 and Johansson's on B013 and B025.
